name: Sable Freight Thermal Henley
description:
A long-sleeve thermal henley from Sable Freight, a workwear brand that started supplying cold-chain logistics workers and has since expanded into general industrial apparel. The fabric is a waffle-knit thermal cotton-poly in off-white, heather grey, or dark brown, with a three-button placket at the neck and flat-locked seams throughout to reduce pressure points under heavier outerwear. The cuffs are slightly extended to stay tucked into gloves.

This is a base layer that gets worn as an outer layer because it looks like one. The cut is relaxed enough to be comfortable over a full shift and fitted enough not to bunch under a jacket. Sable Freight henleys show up in fabrication plants, on delivery crews, and in the kitchens of Tier 2 restaurants. They also show up on Tier 3 people who want something that looks like it works for a living.
what_it_says: You're practical, you run cold, and you've probably had this shirt for at least two years.
worn_by: Tier 3 people who like the aesthetic
story_hooks: Sable Freight's main client is a cold-storage corponation that uses the brand's uniform program to track worker movement — the henleys have no tech, but the belt clips distributed alongside them do.
A Tier 3 designer has been photographed repeatedly in a Sable Freight henley, and now the brand is getting orders it doesn't know how to handle from a demographic it never targeted.
A character wearing a Sable Freight henley is mistaken for a maintenance worker in a restricted facility — and decides to play along.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian long-sleeve henley with honest, no-frills proportions. The relaxed cut reads as hardworking and unpretentious—the kind of garment that moves with the body rather than defining it. On-body, it projects competence and durability without affectation.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso with tapered sleeves; designed for layering but worn standalone. The cut accommodates movement and bulk underneath without excess fabric. Slightly dropped shoulders suggest industrial utility rather than fashion.
physical_description.primary_material: Waffle-knit thermal cotton-poly blend—breathable yet insulating, designed for temperature regulation in climate-controlled logistics and food service environments.
physical_description.texture: Soft waffle-knit surface with visible grid pattern. Flat-locked seams create smooth interior against skin; no raised stitching to catch or irritate during long shifts.
physical_description.color_scheme: Available in off-white, heather grey, or dark brown. Neutral palette signals function over fashion. Minimal branding—small woven Sable Freight label at hem.
physical_description.closures: Three-button henley placket at neckline; buttons are utilitarian plastic composites in matching tone.
distinctive_features: Extended cuffs designed to tuck into work gloves without riding up
Flat-locked seams throughout to reduce pressure points under heavy outerwear
Waffle-knit thermal construction visible at fabric surface
Minimal branding; authenticity through understated labeling
Cut calibrated for both base-layer functionality and standalone wear
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2–3 crossover. Worn authentically by cold-chain and food service workers (Tier 3). Adopted by Tier 2 professionals and affluent Tier 3 who appreciate functional design without conspicuous branding.
physical_description.cultural_context: Marks the wearer as someone engaged in physical, temperature-dependent labor—logistics, manufacturing, professional kitchens. Also signals anti-fashion sensibility among educated consumers who value durability and honest design.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn in and broken-in. Cuffs show faint discoloration from repeated glove friction. Fabric softens with washing. Seams remain flat and intact even after hundreds of shifts.
